title: Why starting to invest at 22 beats starting at 32
description: Case study: the same monthly contribution made ten years apart, and the gap that only shows up at retirement.
angle: Two identical contributions, two radically different outcomes, with the arithmetic made visible.
hook_direction: Start with the number that ends the story: how much more the early starter ends up with.

title: What an index fund actually owns
description: Plain-language look inside a total-market index fund and why that basket grows on its own.
angle: Reveal the invisible contents of a single investment vehicle most people already own.
hook_direction: Ask the audience to picture what they actually own when they 'buy the market'.

title: The expense that quietly eats 40% of an average salary
description: Silent wealth killer: one recurring household line that leaves almost nothing behind, costed out in yearly and lifetime terms.
angle: Treat a single recurring expense as an unseen leak draining the paycheck in real time.
hook_direction: Open by revealing the lifetime total of a cost the owner pays without ever multiplying it out.

title: Why your savings account is slowly shrinking
description: Silent wealth killer: what inflation does to cash sitting still, told as a losing race between two powers.
angle: Show purchasing power being eroded in the background while the account balance still looks healthy.
hook_direction: Lead with the mental image of money melting while the account number stays reassuringly the same.

title: Why winners sell too early and losers hold too long
description: Money behavior: loss aversion turning ordinary investors into bad decision-makers with their own money.
angle: Read the investor's own behavior as the culprit, with a familiar self-inflicted mistake as the evidence.
hook_direction: Ask the audience to guess what their own last trade or sale would have looked like.

title: How a raise quietly upgraded your expenses
description: Money behavior: lifestyle inflation absorbing an income increase so net wealth never moves.
angle: Trace a single raise through spending habits to show where the extra money went.
hook_direction: Reveal the raise on a payslip and follow the money as it disappears into the month.

title: The 24 hours that reset your entire budget
description: Actionable blueprint: a two-part system that makes the first days of the month matter instead of ruining the month.
angle: Hand the viewer one concrete payday system to install immediately.
hook_direction: Present the blueprint up front as a single change to try this week.

title: Split your paycheck the day you get paid
description: Actionable blueprint: a fixed allocation between spending, saving, and investing, done automatically on payday.
angle: Offer a single repeatable money move the viewer can automate before the month starts.
hook_direction: Open with the instruction itself: what to do in the first ten minutes after payday.

title: The skill ladder behind a second income
description: Asymmetric upside: how one narrow, learnable skill can be sold repeatedly while a salary stays intact.
angle: Show the bounded downside of a side skill against the open-ended upside of sellable work.
hook_direction: Contrast the worst case of trying it with the best case, then let the asymmetry speak.

title: Autopsy: the family that spent six figures and saved nothing
description: Case study: a household budget post-mortem showing where the money went and which habits were responsible.
angle: Autopsy a real budget and expose the two decisions that consumed the entire year of savings.
hook_direction: Open with the fact that they earned well and still have nothing, then ask how.

title: Autopsy: the startup salary that disappeared in a funding winter
description: Case study: equity that was promised on paper and what actually happened when growth stalled.
angle: Dissect an equity grant from promise to outcome, showing where the value went.
hook_direction: Lead with the offer letter figure and end on what it was actually worth.

title: Myth: your employer match is free money you can keep
description: Money myth: what an employer match really is, and the vesting rule that decides when it is yours.
angle: Correct the 'free money' belief by introducing the vesting condition hidden in plain sight.
hook_direction: Start from the widely repeated claim, then reveal the clause that undercuts it.
